decision_context.selection_rationale: Inter-service integrations require decoupled retries and delayed processing tolerance, favoring queued async delivery.
decision_context.naming_convention_summary: Contract names and event subjects are stable nouns with version suffixes managed by compatibility policy.
decision_context.threshold_method_summary: Consumer lag, retry, and queue depth thresholds are derived from end-to-end SLA and recovery-time objectives.

threshold_policy.latency_target_derivation: End-to-end latency target is derived from business process SLA, not single request time.
threshold_policy.availability_target_derivation: Availability is defined as successful eventual processing within SLA window.
threshold_policy.timeout_budget_derivation: Producer timeout and consumer visibility timeout are derived from processing time distribution.
threshold_policy.capacity_headroom_derivation: Queue headroom is set using peak event burst and replay/recovery traffic assumptions.
threshold_policy.payload_limit_derivation: Message size limits are derived from broker constraints and serialization overhead.
threshold_policy.concurrency_limit_derivation: Consumer concurrency is set by downstream throughput and lock/contention profiles.
threshold_policy.retry_backoff_derivation: Retry and dead-letter thresholds are derived from transient failure probability and idempotency guarantees.
threshold_policy.delivery_semantics_derivation: Delivery semantics define at-least-once behavior with explicit deduplication strategy.
